key_insight: Autoregressive synthetic EHR generators should undergo patient-level memorisation audits alongside aggregate privacy evaluations.
clinical_relevance: These audits could reveal patient-specific privacy risks that similarity-based checks and aggregate metrics may miss.
method: Compare membership-inference evaluation practices across four autoregressive EHR generators.
Test patient-trajectory reconstruction from partial context.
Use randomly assigned patient-level canaries to separate memorisation from clinical generalisation.
evidence_signal: In a GPT-2-style model deliberately overfit to 1,000 MIMIC-IV patient trajectories, training-patient canaries were systematically recovered and reconstruction approached perfect accuracy as context increased, unlike held-out patients.
watch_item: This deliberately overfit positive-control experiment does not establish privacy risk or audit performance in realistically trained models.
paper_title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
